title: Remove all whitespace from a string using `chars().filter(c -> !Character.isWhitespace(c))` and `Collectors.joining()`.
shortTitle: Remove all whitespace from a string using chars().filter and Collectors.joining()
keyPoints: chars() returns an IntStream of Unicode code points; filter with !Character.isWhitespace removes all whitespace
mapToObj(c -> String.valueOf((char) c)) converts each surviving code point to a one-character string
Collectors.joining() with no argument concatenates with no separator to rebuild the cleaned string
Character.isWhitespace is Unicode-aware and covers spaces, tabs, newlines, and other whitespace forms
The regex alternative s.replaceAll("\\s+", "") is shorter but the stream approach accepts any predicate
This filter-map-join pattern is the standard idiom for rebuilding a string from filtered characters

s1_definition.oneliner: Stream the characters with chars(), filter out whitespace with !Character.isWhitespace, map each code point to a one-character string, and join with no separator.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **chars()** returns IntStream of char values as int.
- **filter(!isWhitespace)** keeps only non-whitespace characters.
- **mapToObj(c -> String.valueOf((char) c))** converts each code point to a one-character string.
- **Collectors.joining()** concatenates with no separator, rebuilding a whitespace-free string.
- **Character.isWhitespace** is Unicode-aware and broader than just the space character.
s1_definition.analogy: Priya at the National Bank of India receives account codes with accidental spaces and tabs like SAV 2001, and squeezes out every blank to produce SAV2001 for storage and validation.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  String: "SAV 2001\tHDFC \n"
       │
       │  .chars()  → IntStream [83, 65, 86, 32, 50, ...]
       │
       │  .filter(!isWhitespace)
       ▼
  IntStream [83, 65, 86, 50, 48, 48, 49, 72, 68, 70, 67]
       │       S   A   V   2   0   0   1   H   D   F   C
       │
       │  .mapToObj(c -> String.valueOf((char) c))
       ▼
  Stream<String> ["S","A","V","2","0","0","1","H","D","F","C"]
       │
       │  .collect(Collectors.joining())
       ▼
  "SAV2001HDFC"
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
To strip all whitespace with streams, take the characters with chars(), filter out whitespace using the negation of Character.isWhitespace, map each surviving code point to a one-character string, and join with the no-argument joining to rebuild a clean string. For a code like "SAV 2001 HDFC", this drops all spaces and tabs to produce SAV2001HDFC.

Character.isWhitespace is Unicode-aware and catches far more than the plain space character: tabs, newlines, and other whitespace forms. This matters for real input at the National Bank of India where account codes arrive with accidental spacing before validation and storage.

The stream approach earns its keep when the filtering rule is more complex than whitespace, because you just swap the predicate and the same filter-map-join shape rebuilds the sanitized string. For the specific case of whitespace alone, the concise regex replaceAll is often clearer.

Remember one sentence: chars(), filter(!isWhitespace), mapToObj to String, and joining() is the standard stream idiom for stripping characters and rebuilding a cleaned string.
